telemetry.label: Help improve Loop
telemetry.on: On — reports when a race starts and ends.

vrOverlay.label: VR overlay
vrOverlay.detected: iRacing running in VR — the headset panels are active.
vrOverlay.notDetected: iRacing is not in VR right now. On automatic, the panels turn on by themselves when it launches in a headset.

monitorOverlayInVr.label: Monitor overlay while in VR
monitorOverlayInVr.on: On — the tower also shows on the monitor, for streaming or recording.
monitorOverlayInVr.off: Off — in VR the monitor does not draw the tower (you would not see it from inside the headset).

spotter.label: Loop spotter
spotter.on: On — the iRacing spotter stays quiet while Loop is open, and goes back to normal when you close it.
spotter.off: Off — the iRacing spotter talks normally.
spotter.semAppIni: The iRacing app.ini was not found.

autoPaint.label: Paint my car in the team's color
autoPaint.on: On — when you export the round, your car gets the team color in the iRacing garage. Any paint already there is kept alongside it, ending in .loop-bak. If you use Trading Paints, its paint wins.
autoPaint.off: Off — Loop leaves your car paint alone.

spotterVoz.label: Spotter voice
spotterVoz.on: On — the spotter checks in when you get in the car and calls out cars alongside.
spotterVoz.off: Off — calls only show up on the overlay strip.

volumeRadio.label: Radio volume
volumeRadio.hint: Applies to the spotter and the engineer alike — they are the same person.

autoYellow.label: Automatic yellow flag
autoYellow.notFound: iRacing not found on this PC.
autoYellow.on: On — throws a yellow automatically in crashes against the AI.
autoYellow.off: Throws a yellow flag automatically in crashes against the AI.

iracingDiag.title: iRacing diagnostics
iracingDiag.desc: Checks the connection to the simulator and generates a log for bug reports.
iracingDiag.sendPrivacy: Sends the tail of the log, the app version and the result of this check. Your Windows username is stripped from file paths. Nothing is sent unless you click.
iracingDiag.sentTicket: Sent. Include this code in your report:

veredito.so_launcher: Only the iRacing interface is open.
veredito.sessao_nao_pronta: Simulator connecting — session not ready yet.
veredito.acesso_negado: Windows denied access to the simulator's memory.
veredito.sim_sem_sdk: Simulator open, but it is not publishing telemetry.
veredito.nao_suportado: The iRacing SDK only works on Windows.

acao.ok: Nothing to do. If a screen still shows zeros, copy the log and include it in your report.
acao.sim_fechado: Normal state. Open the simulator and join a session for Loop to start reading.
acao.so_launcher: Normal state. The interface alone publishes no data — get on track to connect.
acao.sessao_nao_pronta: Wait a few seconds on track and check again.
acao.acesso_negado: This happens when the simulator runs as administrator and Loop does not. Close Loop and reopen it with right-click → Run as administrator.
acao.sim_sem_sdk: Check whether your antivirus is blocking Loop and whether the simulator is up to date. Copy the log and include it in your report.
acao.nao_suportado: No action available on this system.

debug.macroNote2: . iRacing rewrites app.ini on close — so edit it with the sim closed. Backup at
debug.chatDesc: Sends free text to the iRacing chat (focuses the window, opens chat and types). With the sim open in a session with AI.
debug.breakdownDesc1: Arms a guaranteed failure on YOUR car. With the sim open in a running session, click and cross the line — the monitor fires the
debug.breakdownDesc2: on its own on the next lap.
debug.armedMyCar: Armed! Cross the finish line — the breakdown fires on its own on the next lap.
debug.armFailed: Couldn't arm: join an iRacing session (your car number needs to be visible).
debug.armedGrid: Grid armed! With the race running, cars will drop parts over the next few laps (1 every ~1.5s to avoid spamming).
debug.radioDesc: Shows a sample card cycling in the center of the screen (over the game), so you can find and position the radio overlay without waiting for a real breakdown. Remember to turn it off afterward.
debug.captureDesc: Saves ALL live race telemetry (+ session YAML + history) to a file, to calibrate the app with real track data. Dev only — not part of the commercial game.
debug.capturing: Recording… join an iRacing session. File: {{path}}
debug.calendarDesc: Pick which calendar to use. V3 is the newest; V2 and Legacy stay as fallback.

engenheiroPtt.label: Race engineer radio
engenheiroPtt.on: On — hold the button and ask; the engineer answers out loud.
engenheiroPtt.off: Off — the engineer does not answer questions.
engenheiroPtt.semGatilho: No button bound — there is no way to call the engineer.
engenheiroPtt.pressioneTecla: Press the key you want to use. Escape cancels.
engenheiroPtt.pressioneBotao: Press the button on your wheel. {{n}} game device(s) found.

teste.label: Test the radio
teste.desc: Checks the wheel, the microphone, and both together — no need to have iRacing open.
teste.semDispositivo: Windows sees no game device. Turn the wheel on before opening Loop.
teste.nenhumBotao: Press any button on the wheel.
teste.segureEFale: Hold the bound button and speak. On release, the recording plays here.
teste.curta: Too short to count as a question — hold the button while speaking.
teste.modo_eco_desc: Records and plays back. Proves the hardware, no server involved.
teste.modo_cadeia_desc: The real pipeline, step by step. A typed question skips only transcription — it lets you test the recorded pack with no server up.
teste.semRastro: Type a question above, or hold the button and speak.
teste.forcarModelo: Force the model — bypasses the recorded pack and hits the server, even with no session (uses demo facts).
teste.avisoSemTelemetria: With no session open the recorded pack always answers "no car data" — that is correct behaviour, not a failure. Tick "Force the model" above to reach the server with demo facts.

engenheiroPtt.microfoneSumiu: The chosen microphone did not respond. Recording through {{rotulo}}.
engenheiroPtt.microfoneNaoAberto: Not open yet — opens when a session starts, or when you test the radio.

iracingSemDados.aviso: Loop has not been able to read iRacing even once since the app started — this screen may be empty because of that, not because of what happened in the race. Check Settings › iRacing diagnostics.

redemption.detailDnf: a DNF in the last race{{track}}
redemption.detailDismal: a result well below your usual (P{{pos}})
redemption.statement: Central hook — REACTION. The driver comes off {{detail}} and this round is about responding, flipping the switch and getting the campaign back on track. The whole weekend reads from that recent stumble.

title_defense.chaser: The direct chaser is {{gap}} point(s) behind.
title_defense.setback: — and you arrive right after a DNF, which makes the defense even more delicate
title_defense.statement: Central hook — LEAD DEFENSE. You reach {{track}} atop the championship{{setback}}.{{chaser}} The round is about managing the pressure and leaving here still setting the pace, giving no opening.

title_chase.statement: Central hook — TITLE CHASE. You're {{gap}} point(s) off the leader{{leader}}, with {{rounds}} round(s) to go. This is a real chance to close the gap — the round is worth a direct fight at the top.

nemesis.label: ("{{label}}")
nemesis.statement: Central hook — PERSONAL DUEL. Your nemesis {{name}}{{label}} is on this grid.{{h2h}} The weekend revolves around this clash: he's the yardstick for your round.

pressure.statement: Central hook — GROUND UNDER THREAT. The table has tightened behind you{{gap}}. This round is about protecting your championship band: you can't afford a passive weekend.

track_trauma.statement: Central hook — UNFINISHED BUSINESS. {{track}} has open history with you ({{detail}}). The axis is respect and clean execution: here, erring little is worth more than attacking too much.

track_fortress.statement: Central hook — YOUR KIND OF TRACK. {{track}} holds good memories (best result P{{best}}). The weekend starts with the track in your favor — the read can be bolder.

weather.statement: Central hook — WEATHER LOTTERY. The forecast is for a {{clima}} track, and that scrambles the grid and decides the race. The axis is cool reading: the track will reward whoever errs least, not whoever attacks most.

breakdown.statement: Central hook — MECHANICAL FRAGILITY. The car arrives with {{level}} breakdown risk{{parts}}. It's risk, not certainty: the weekend's axis is weighing attack against reliability, and maybe sparing the car.

grand_stage.statement: Central hook — THE STAGE. {{occasion}}{{audience}}. The showcase and pressure weigh beyond the table: the axis is the occasion, and what it demands of whoever's at its center.

debut.statement: Central hook — FRESH START. Season opener at {{track}}: table reset, the whole grid starts from zero. The round is about building the campaign's foundation and turning preseason expectation into real points.

baseline.statement: Central hook — BANK AND BUILD. With no dominant storyline, {{track}} is a round to score big, gain table position and avoid silly losses. The axis is competitive consistency.

stageAppendix.text: And it's no ordinary stage: {{occasion}}{{audience}} — the occasion amplifies everything at stake.

form.noStanding: The team wants to turn practice pace into a clean result.
form.recent: In the three most recent reads you're coming off {{list}}.
form.noTrend: The recent run hasn't set a clear trend yet.

redemption.lead_0: The last race left a mark, and {{trackName}} arrives as the round for the response. The whole weekend organizes around a simple idea: getting the campaign back on track.
redemption.lead_1: After the recent stumble, the team treats {{trackName}} as a turning point. It's not about forgetting what happened — it's about turning frustration into clean execution.
redemption.outlook_0: The plan isn't heroics: it's a solid race, no new mistakes, that gives the garage its confidence back. {{formSentence}}
redemption.outlook_1: The priority is to stop the bleeding and leave here with real points. {{formSentence}}
redemption.quote_0: We know what happened. Now it's a cool head, a clean race and starting to score again.
redemption.quote_1: Page turned. {{trackName}} is where our response begins.

title_defense.lead_0: You reach {{trackName}} atop the championship, and that changes the weight of every detail. The round is less about attacking and more about not giving up what's already yours.
title_defense.lead_1: Being on top turns {{trackName}} into a test of cool blood. The weekend's job is to leave here still setting the pace.
title_defense.outlook_0: Control the pressure, manage risk and protect the margin — you don't have to win to win. {{formSentence}}
title_defense.outlook_1: A high, clean result keeps the season's architecture intact. {{formSentence}}
title_defense.quote_0: We came in to defend what's ours. Head in place and the lead stays with us.
title_defense.quote_1: Leading demands composure. That's what we'll deliver here.

title_chase.lead_0: {{gapToLeader}} point(s) from {{leaderName}} and with {{remainingRounds}} round(s) to go, {{trackName}} becomes a real chance to move the table. The title math is still alive.
title_chase.lead_1: The championship is still within reach, and {{trackName}} is the kind of round that decides title chases. Every point on {{leaderName}} matters from here on.
title_chase.outlook_0: The message is controlled aggression: go for the front without wrecking the race. {{formSentence}}
title_chase.outlook_1: Closing for good demands a strong, clean Sunday. {{formSentence}}
title_chase.quote_0: We're close. This isn't the time for anxiety — it's the time to close in.
title_chase.quote_1: The gap exists, but we can cut it here. Let's go for it with sense.

nemesis.lead_0: {{nemesisName}} is on this grid, and it's impossible to separate your round from that clash. {{trackName}} becomes the stage for a duel that already has history.
nemesis.lead_1: Every season has a rivalry that defines races, and yours is here at {{trackName}}. {{nemesisName}} is the yardstick for your weekend.
nemesis.outlook_0: Beating the direct rival is worth more than the position on paper — but without letting the duel cost the race. {{formSentence}}
nemesis.outlook_1: The focus is winning the direct comparison and coming out on top. {{formSentence}}
nemesis.quote_0: We know exactly who we're fighting. This one's personal, and we want to win.
nemesis.quote_1: There's a showdown set here. That's what a good race is made of.

pressure.lead_0: The table has tightened behind you, and {{trackName}} leaves no room for a passive weekend. The round is about defending your championship band.
pressure.lead_1: With the gap ever shorter, {{trackName}} demands an immediate response. You can't passively manage what the table is demanding.
pressure.outlook_0: Race with clarity, no waste, and keep the standings from tightening further. {{formSentence}}
pressure.outlook_1: Scoring big here became a must, not a luxury. {{formSentence}}
pressure.quote_0: The margin got thin. The answer needs to show up now, in this race.
pressure.quote_1: We can't deliver a routine weekend at this point.

weather.lead_0: The {{climaLabel}} forecast turns {{trackName}} into a race of reading, not bravado. The weather can rewrite the grid from start to finish.
weather.lead_1: When the track goes wet, {{trackName}} stops being predictable. The weather comes in as a real distortion factor for the round.
weather.outlook_0: The track will reward whoever errs least, not whoever attacks most. Surviving the chaos well already changes the race. {{formSentence}}
weather.outlook_1: Composure above all: a clean result here can be worth more than it seems. {{formSentence}}
weather.quote_0: With this weather, the race is in your head. Fewer mistakes, more patience.
weather.quote_1: Rain levels the grid. We read the race and take the opening.

track_trauma.lead_0: {{trackName}} is no ordinary track for you — the history here calls for caution before any bold promise. Clean execution is worth more than bravado.
track_trauma.lead_1: The recent memory of {{trackName}} advises prudence. The round arrives with a clear warning: here, erring little is the way.
track_trauma.outlook_0: Discipline from start to finish, without forcing what the track usually charges dearly for. {{formSentence}}
track_trauma.outlook_1: The goal is to break the record with a mature race. {{formSentence}}
track_trauma.quote_0: This track has cost us dearly before. This time, it's focus and discipline.
track_trauma.quote_1: We know the history here. No taking it easy.

track_fortress.lead_0: {{trackName}} holds good memories of yours, and that allows a bolder read of the round. The track plays in your favor from the first practice.
track_fortress.lead_1: Few tracks suit you as well as {{trackName}}. The record here gives grounds to attack with legitimate ambition.
track_fortress.outlook_0: The question is turning past reference into present result. {{formSentence}}
track_fortress.outlook_1: With the track in your favor, you can think big without illusion. {{formSentence}}
track_fortress.quote_0: We like it here. Time to turn that good memory into points.
track_fortress.quote_1: This track suits us. Let's make the most of it.

breakdown.lead_0: The car reaches {{trackName}} with real breakdown risk, and that changes the weekend's math. It's risk, not certainty — but it weighs on every decision.
breakdown.lead_1: Mechanical fragility is the topic at {{trackName}}. The round becomes a balance between attack and preserving the car to the flag.
breakdown.outlook_0: It may be worth easing off at times to guarantee the finish. {{formSentence}}
breakdown.outlook_1: Reaching the end intact may be worth more than risking it all. {{formSentence}}
breakdown.quote_0: The car needs attention. We'll weigh every attack against the risk of not finishing.
breakdown.quote_1: Better a guaranteed point than a heroic zero. Cool heads here.

grand_stage.lead_0: {{eventOccasion}} puts {{trackName}} under the spotlights. The showcase and pressure weigh beyond the points at stake.
grand_stage.lead_1: Not every race carries the weight of {{trackName}} on this occasion. It's the kind of round that separates those who rise from those who shrink.
grand_stage.outlook_0: The stage demands presence: delivering under pressure is half the story here. {{formSentence}}
grand_stage.outlook_1: Big occasions remember whoever showed up. {{formSentence}}
grand_stage.quote_0: A round like this we mark in memory. We came to show up.
grand_stage.quote_1: The stage is big. It's exactly where we want to be.

debut.lead_0: The season begins at {{trackName}} with the whole grid starting from zero. There's no table to defend — there's an entire campaign to build.
debut.lead_1: {{trackName}} restarts everything: table reset and the first read of the year's forces. The round is about planting the season's foundation.
debut.outlook_0: A solid start avoids having to play catch-up right off the bat. {{formSentence}}
debut.outlook_1: Starting well at the opener gives a confidence base for the rest of the calendar. {{formSentence}}
debut.quote_0: New season, clean slate. We want to start on the right foot.
debut.quote_1: It's time to turn the preseason into real points.

baseline.lead_0: With no dominant storyline, {{trackName}} is a building round: score big, gain position and avoid silly losses. Consistency is the name of the game.
baseline.lead_1: {{trackName}} brings no big table drama, and that's fine. The round is about doing the simple things well and growing in the championship.
baseline.outlook_0: A clean, efficient race here eases the season's breathing. {{formSentence}}
baseline.outlook_1: Every point banked without scares reorganizes the campaign around you. {{formSentence}}
baseline.quote_0: No inventing. Clean race, points in the bag and we keep growing.
baseline.quote_1: Focus on the basics done well. That's how a season is built.

expectation.p1-controlled-1: Arrives as the round's main reference, riding the most solid run among the front names.
expectation.p1-controlled-2: Opens the weekend as the grid's benchmark, backed by a spell that keeps delivering control and big points.
expectation.p1-charging-1: Leads the favorites' line with high morale, bringing the recent pace of someone who knows how to control the front of the weekend.
expectation.p1-charging-2: Takes on the role of the man to beat this round, supported by a strong upward trend over the last races.
expectation.p1-volatile-1: Remains the natural reference of the round, but the paddock wants to see that speed turn into a clean race from start to finish.
expectation.p1-volatile-2: Still arrives as a central name up front, though he carries a clear message: turn pace into error-free execution.
expectation.p1-stable-1: Enters the round as the axis of the fight, with a campaign steady enough to set the tone for the front runners.
expectation.p1-stable-2: Remains the grid's most reliable reference, even without opening an absolute margin over his immediate chasers.
expectation.p1-baseline-1: Arrives as the round's heaviest sporting name, with enough championship reading to command the front.
expectation.p1-baseline-2: Starts as the natural reference of the weekend, backed by the strongest mix of points, pace and front-running presence.
expectation.p2-controlled-1: Enters the weekend with a clear front-row read, sustained by strong results and little margin for error.
expectation.p2-controlled-2: Arrives as the round's most consistent direct chaser, with a real package to push the favorite from the start.
expectation.p2-charging-1: Appears as the name most ready to attack the front, riding a clearly visible recent growth curve.
expectation.p2-charging-2: Brings a real case to press for the front, with form on the rise and the pace to shake up the round's hierarchy.
expectation.p2-volatile-1: Has the speed to run on the front row, but still needs to convert that performance ceiling into a clean Sunday.
expectation.p2-volatile-2: Arrives with a real read to attack the front, provided he can stabilize a campaign that still alternates peaks and slips.
expectation.p2-stable-1: Holds a strong front-row candidacy, backed by recent regularity and constant presence in the front block.
expectation.p2-stable-2: Enters as a credentialed chaser of the round, with enough consistency to press the top if qualifying falls into place.
expectation.p2-baseline-1: Begins the weekend as a firm front-row name, carrying the material to bother the front runners.
expectation.p2-baseline-2: Opens the round with a real attacking credential, backed by a package that keeps him near the championship leaders.
expectation.p3-controlled-1: Reaches the podium block with a strong technical base, backed by recent results that keep him near the front.
expectation.p3-controlled-2: Enters as a serious name for the podium, sustained by a clean, competitive recent campaign.
expectation.p3-charging-1: Has been growing in the fight up front and appears as a real candidate to reach this round's podium.
expectation.p3-charging-2: The recent trend places him inside the hottest podium block, with clear room to grow over the weekend.
expectation.p3-volatile-1: Has the ceiling to get into the podium, but the paddock's read still runs through turning speed into consistency.
expectation.p3-volatile-2: Emerges with top-3 potential, though he still carries a dose of instability that demands a well-executed race.
expectation.p3-stable-1: Recent consistency keeps him on the podium radar, even without the same raw ceiling of the two strongest names.
expectation.p3-stable-2: Arrives as a firm presence in the front block, with enough repertoire to sustain a podium race.
expectation.p3-baseline-1: Starts as a legitimate podium candidate, with a campaign strong enough to run in the same conversation as the favorites.
expectation.p3-baseline-2: Opens the round within the podium bracket, backed by a solid mix of points, pace and front-running presence.
expectation.p4-controlled-1: Appears as a real threat to the top 5, with a recent base clean enough to punish any mistake up front.
expectation.p4-controlled-2: Arrives a step below the podium block, but with the consistency to steal heavy points if the race opens up.
expectation.p4-charging-1: Is on the rise and enters as a dangerous name to cut through the top 5 if the race goes off script.
expectation.p4-charging-2: The recent growth curve makes him a concrete threat to the more established names up front.
expectation.p4-volatile-1: Has the speed to infiltrate the round's high block, but still carries a riskier read than his direct rivals.
expectation.p4-volatile-2: Emerges as the grid's aggressive card: interesting ceiling, though execution still swings too much to trust blindly.
expectation.p4-stable-1: Occupies the second front pack with consistency, ready to capitalize on any race that breaks among the favorites.
expectation.p4-stable-2: Keeps a strong secondary-threat profile, sustained by enough regularity to score big if the round scrambles.
expectation.p4-baseline-1: Enters as a dangerous name to stretch the top-5 fight, especially if the weekend opens up space at the front.
expectation.p4-baseline-2: Opens the round as a well-positioned secondary threat, with a package to turn chaos into big points.
expectation.p5-controlled-1: Runs on the outside, but arrives with a base clean enough to enter the big-points radar early.
expectation.p5-controlled-2: Appears as a well-organized outsider of the round, with recent consistency to bother the top 5.
expectation.p5-charging-1: Is climbing at the right moment and emerges as the liveliest outsider to surprise in the race's main block.
expectation.p5-charging-2: The recent trend keeps him outside only on paper, because his pace already puts him on the round's radar.
expectation.p5-volatile-1: Arrives as a surprise name, still trying to trade swings for a race that truly puts him in the front conversation.
expectation.p5-volatile-2: Has room to show up well above expectations, but his recent campaign still mixes bright flashes with avoidable losses.
expectation.p5-stable-1: Remains outside the main hierarchy, but with enough regularity to seize any top-5 opportunity.
expectation.p5-stable-2: Enters the radar as a competitive outsider, backed by a run that keeps him near the round's strong block.
expectation.p5-baseline-1: Runs on the outside, but can turn into a real surprise if he repeats his recent level when the race tightens.
expectation.p5-baseline-2: Opens the round in the paddock's watch group, with room to grow if the favorites leave a gap.

header.title: Return to the paddock.
header.subtitle: Pick an existing save to continue your journey, review the grid, and head straight to the next race.

library.note: Each save opens straight into the current dashboard.

empty.title: No career found
empty.subtitle: Create your first career to start filling the paddock.

backups.title: Career backups
backups.subtitle: Every season rollover creates an automatic backup. Restoring rolls the whole save back to that point — it isn't a merge.
backups.empty: No backups yet. The first one shows up once you advance a season.

createConfirm.title: Create a backup of season {{season}}?
createConfirm.body: There is a single backup per season. If this season already has one, it will be overwritten and cannot be recovered.

restoreConfirm.title: Restore season {{season}}?
restoreConfirm.body: All progress made after that point will be lost — database, results and context roll back to that season. A copy of the current state is kept in career.db.bak, but there is only one slot: a second restore replaces it.

rivalryPerception.title: Perceived rivalries (debug)
rivalryPerception.descPre: Runs rivalry perception on a race (live or saved) for a probe car. Only shows what the system
rivalryPerception.emptyLive: No live race on the monitor. Race (or spectate) a session in iRacing, or pick a saved race.
rivalryPerception.emptySaved: This saved race has no field trace.
rivalryPerception.noRivalries: No rivalry perceived in this race for this car.

rosterGen.title: Generate AI Roster (career → iRacing)
rosterGen.subtitle: Writes the career grid as an iRacing AI roster — the drivers come in with our names, attributes and team color.
rosterGen.connectionTitle: Automatic detection — turns on by itself when iRacing opens
rosterGen.noSaves: No save found. Create a career first.
rosterGen.testSeasonTitle: BLANK season (no results) with race 1 using the scripted weather of the 1st race — to preview the script in the iRacing menu.
rosterGen.rainTestTitle: Generates 3 seasons (Dry/Wet/Storm) with 16 controlled drivers (4 skills × 4 rain factors) — driver_skill already comes in re-ranked by per-driver rain. Run all 3 with the AI and compare the results.
rosterGen.previewTitleAttr: Rebuilds the result of the LAST race run in iRacing as the career would see it (positions, grid, fastest lap, DNFs) — WITHOUT saving anything. Validate against the iRacing screen before enabling persistence.
rosterGen.dumpYamlTitle: Writes the iRacing session YAML to a file (%TEMP%/loop_session_dump.yaml) to inspect the official results (ResultsPositions) and qualifying.
rosterGen.trackOverrideTitle: Optional: track ID to force the skill margin (testing). Empty = auto-aim at the NEXT race on the calendar.
rosterGen.rainTestIntro: Load each one in iRacing, let the AI race and compare the results. Effective skill (already with rain) of each driver:
rosterGen.rainValidationMid: the order follows skill (Alien-* wins). In the
rosterGen.rainValidationTail: (higher effective skill). If that happens on track, the rain system works.
rosterGen.previewValidation: 🔑 Compare with the iRacing result screen: positions, grid, fastest lap (🟣) and retirements. If it matches, the bridge is correct and we can enable persistence in the career.
rosterGen.paintApplyOnce: Apply once — your car ends up matching your teammate's.
rosterGen.custidCapturedTail: while you race (the monitor reads the session and stores it). This button just confirms what was already captured. It's the basis for your car's automatic paint.
rosterGen.paintCarBtn: 🎨 Paint my car in the team color
rosterGen.paintCloseWarning: ⚠️ Close iRacing first (it reads the paints on open / when entering the garage). You need "Show custom paints" enabled.
rosterGen.finalWarning: ⚠️ Open iRacing after generating (it reads the rosters on startup). The player is excluded from the roster — they drive, they don't become AI.

postRacePanel.title: Post-Race — Analysis
postRacePanel.subtitle: Race trace, gap to leader and lap-by-lap pace consistency.
postRacePanel.noLapsYet: No laps recorded yet. The history is built live during the race — it shows up here on its own as the laps go by.
postRacePanel.fewLaps: Too few laps recorded to trace. Lap by lap appears as the leader completes each lap.
postRacePanel.clippedNote: Gaps above {{cap}}s were clipped at the top (cars far behind, stopped in the pits or disqualified) to keep the pack readable.
postRacePanel.noYourLaps: None of your laps recorded yet.
postRacePanel.noBattleData: No battle data yet. It's sampled ~1×/second while you race.
postRacePanel.battleNote: Gaps above {{cap}}s are flattened at the top/bottom. Sections with no line = you leading (no one ahead) or last.

radio.chatBlockedText: I can't send commands to iRacing. Run the sim in WINDOWED or BORDERLESS mode (exclusive fullscreen blocks it).

positionPanel.title: VR OVERLAY — POSITION
positionPanel.radioHintPre: The radio only appears with a breakdown — turn on
positionPanel.radioHintPost: in Settings to see and position it now.
positionPanel.recenterTooltip: Places the overlay in front of you, at the configured position, from where you're looking now
positionPanel.recenterKeyHint: Tip: use the SAME key as iRacing's "Center VR" (Options → Controls) and one press recenters both. In VR you can also use
positionPanel.padNoDevices: No game device found. Turn the wheel on before capturing — if it doesn't show up in Windows "Game Controllers", Loop can't see it either.
positionPanel.padHint: The wheel button is watched by Loop, not by the VR layer: it works with the app in the background, but the app must be running.

telemetryCockpit.noStrategyData: No strategy data for this race.
telemetryCockpit.noStopSegment: No stops · started and finished on {{compound}} · full race without changing tires

raceCharts.noLaps: No laps recorded for this driver.
raceCharts.rivalIntroPost: — above 0 = rival ahead (you chasing), below = you ahead.

telemetryConsent.title: Help improve Loop
telemetryConsent.body: When you race in iRacing, Loop can let us know the race happened. Added to everyone else's, that shows what actually gets played — and that's what decides what we build first.
telemetryConsent.sends: Race start and end, duration, track and car, where you finished and your best lap, plus your career's year, category and difficulty.
telemetryConsent.never: Your name, your driver's or team's name, anything from your save. Nothing that identifies you.
telemetryConsent.reversible: You can change your mind any time, in Settings › General.

updater.upToDate: You're already on the latest version.

globalTeamRecords.title: Team records
globalTeamRecords.subtitle: Every team that has raced in this scope.
globalTeamRecords.empty: No team has raced in this scope yet.
globalTeamRecords.heading: {{scope}} · {{count}} teams

scopeNote.category: Only {{scope}} races. The team against whoever was on track with it.
scopeNote.group: The numbers cover all of {{scope}}. Equivalent ladders are grouped together to avoid comparing cars from different worlds — a team may have won its titles in one category and race in another today.
scopeNote.world: Every team in the save, across all categories. A Rookie title and a GT3 title weigh the same here — this compares size, not merit.

globalTeamRecords.totalTitle: {{value}} across the whole career, all categories
globalTeamRecords.totalHint: The smaller number beside it is the career total, across all categories.
globalTeamRecords.scopeFamily: In multiclass categories only the {{family}} class counts — the other makes race separate championships within the same category.
